deviations.what: The controller-loaded Dialog fragment is declared in the view's mvc:dependents aggregation and opened 1:1 via follow_up_action( cs_event-control_by_id, settingsDialog open ). confirm/cancel/resetFilters become backend events; confirm forwards the public filterString event parameter (${$parameters>/filterString}) and toasts it together with the slider value, like the original handleConfirm.

The Slider carries a bound value attribute the original does not have: the sample seeds and restores it imperatively (oSlider.setValue in the fragment-load callback, in handleCancel and in handleResetFilters). A bound ABAP field is the abap2UI5 equivalent of all three, so the initial value 50 comes from model_init and cancel/reset just write the field.

ViewSettingsCustomItem carries bound filterCount and selected attributes the original does not have. The original drives both imperatively (setFilterCount/setSelected in handleSliderChange, handleCancel and handleResetFilters); both are ordinary bindable properties, so the port binds them and computes the state in ABAP.

Thin frontend: the comparisons that decide the filter state - new slider value against the last confirmed one (handleSliderChange), and the confirmed value against the reset value 50 (handleCancel) - are computed in ABAP instead of in the controller. filterResetValue/filterPreviousValue become the constant c_reset_value and the protected previous_value; behaviour is identical.
